prompts.text: What is a decision you make almost every morning that quietly affects the rest of your day?
Tell me about a time you changed one small part of your routine and noticed an unexpected difference.
A day can be memorable without anything unusual happening in it.
Imagine you could add one entirely free hour to tomorrow. Where would it actually go?
Being able to start every morning slowly or having a completely flexible finish to every workday?
People often organise their weeks around routines they don't remember choosing.
How do you know when a routine is helping you rather than simply keeping you busy?
You have to explain your normal Tuesday to a visitor from another century. What would confuse them most?
What's a habit you picked up accidentally that eventually became part of who you are?
If you watched a time-lapse of your ordinary week, what pattern would surprise you?
Have you ever made a tiny choice that turned out to change more than you expected?
Tell me about an ordinary meeting or conversation that nudged your life in a different direction.
Most turning points probably look unremarkable while we're living through them.
You find a notebook listing three plans you considered five years ago. Which one would you be most curious to revisit?
Knowing the moment your life took an unexpected direction or discovering how differently it might have gone?
Sometimes you only realise a particular day mattered after looking back several years.
What would you say has changed most about what you consider a good day?
You could briefly revisit one harmless decision from your past without changing it. Which one would you want to understand better?
Tell me about a detour that introduced you to something that later became important.
Is there something you almost didn't do that you're particularly glad you tried?
When you move somewhere new, what makes it start to feel like your own neighbourhood?
Describe a place where you felt unexpectedly comfortable even though it was your first visit.
The people you see in a place often shape your attachment to it more than its appearance.
You're asked to design a welcoming town square for people of very different ages. What's the first feature you add?
Living within walking distance of familiar faces or constantly discovering new corners of a big city?
Some streets become part of our personal history simply because we walk them often.
What's a place you associate with a particular stage of your life, and why?
A friend visits your hometown for the first time and asks what makes it feel special to you. Where do you take them?
Tell me about noticing that somewhere familiar had changed while you had been away.
How much does the sound of a neighbourhood affect whether you enjoy being there?
What sort of object is hardest for you to throw away even after it stops being useful?

prompts.text: How do you recognise personal progress when there isn't a clear finish line?
An ordinary change in how you react can be a bigger achievement than a visible milestone.
You get a letter written by yourself three years ago. What question would you hope your past self had asked?
Making steady progress you barely notice or experiencing one big breakthrough after months of effort?
Tell me about something you can do easily now that once required a lot of concentration.
It's easy to forget improvements when you've already adjusted your expectations.
Has your definition of being successful changed as you got older?
You could display one chart about your life with no numbers related to money. What would it measure?
Describe a small accomplishment you appreciated more because you understood the work behind it.
What's an area of life where getting better actually made you more curious, not less?
What everyday job would you like to observe from behind the scenes for just one day?
You can accompany a lighthouse keeper, a baker or a sound technician for a shift. Whose routine interests you most?
Listening carefully to someone's workday can make an unfamiliar profession fascinating.
Tell me about learning how something ordinary is made and never seeing it quite the same way again.
Spending an afternoon in a busy market's back rooms or watching a theatre prepare for opening night?
Much of what keeps daily life running happens outside most people's view.
Who's someone whose daily routine is so different from yours that you'd genuinely enjoy comparing notes?
Your neighbourhood lets you try any community role for one day. Where would you volunteer?
Describe a conversation with someone that changed how you understood their everyday responsibilities.
What familiar service do you suspect requires far more work than most people realise?
When does an hour feel shortest to you, and when does it feel longest?
Tell me about a day that felt much longer than twenty-four hours for an interesting reason.
Waiting for something can change how we experience it even before it happens.
You could spend one afternoon in a place where nobody could check the time. How would you decide when to leave?
A weekend full of varied activities or one long uninterrupted stretch of free time?
Some years feel crowded with memories while other years seem to pass in a blur.
Are there activities that make you forget to check your phone or watch entirely?
A city decides to close its clocks for one day. What part of everyday life becomes most confusing?
Describe a short moment that you remember in unusually vivid detail.
What would you like to make more time for if nobody expected an explanation?
What's an opinion you've changed after actually experiencing something for yourself?
Being comfortable saying 'I was wrong' can make learning less exhausting.
Someone you respect gives a careful argument against a harmless belief you've held for years. How do you examine it?
Discovering you were wrong through a friendly conversation or through testing the idea yourself?
Tell me about something you once dismissed that later became one of your interests.
People sometimes become more open-minded after finding out how much they still don't know.
What's the difference between being persuaded and simply going along with everyone else?
You find two explanations for the same local tradition and both sound convincing. How would you investigate?
Describe a moment when asking an extra question changed your interpretation of a situation.
Is there a question you enjoy discussing even though you don't expect a final answer?
What's the smallest group of people you've seen build a surprisingly strong sense of community?
A street with ten households wants to organise one shared event. What activity would help everyone participate?
A little regular interaction can make neighbours feel familiar without forcing everyone to be close friends.
Tell me about a group you joined for a practical reason and stayed in because of the people.
A neighbourhood book exchange or an open afternoon where residents share useful skills?
Some communities form around things as simple as taking the same bus or using the same park.
Which shared activity do you think helps strangers cooperate most naturally?
Your neighbourhood has a spare room that anyone can use once a week. What would be a good use for it?
Describe a time a stranger's small gesture made you feel welcome in a new place.
How can a community make room for people who enjoy contributing quietly rather than speaking up?
What ordinary part of life today do you think people will find strange a hundred years from now?
